# Anvia Documentation

> Anvia is a TypeScript runtime and product suite for building, debugging, and operating provider-agnostic AI agents. Applications retain ownership of authentication, permissions, data, persistence, deployment, and user-facing responses.

Use the SDK documentation for runtime APIs and application integration, Studio for local inspection and debugging, and Lens for production observability and evaluation. Package pages describe the public surface of each published `@anvia/*` package. Prefer documented exports over internal source paths.

Choose the narrowest topic guide that covers the task. These guides contain curated implementation context, production boundaries, representative APIs, and links to authoritative pages. Examples are illustrative; verify exact behavior in the relevant SDK and package documentation.

## Topic Guides

- [Agents, tools, and MCP](https://docs.anvia.dev/llms-agents.txt): Models, agents, tools, MCP, skills, memory, agent teams, pipelines versus durable workflows, sandboxing, and streaming.
- [Full-stack applications](https://docs.anvia.dev/llms-apps.txt): `@anvia/server` streaming, `@anvia/react` client state, headless UI, interactions, resumption, durable chat, authentication, cancellation, and Discord/Slack/Telegram channels.
- [Evaluations and observability](https://docs.anvia.dev/llms-evals.txt): Tracing, Lens setup, runtime scoring, evaluation suites, datasets, release comparison, and quality gates, with links to alerts, cost, and testing.
- [RAG, knowledge, and retrieval](https://docs.anvia.dev/llms-rag.txt): Vector indexes, vector stores, embeddings, metadata filters, Neo4j/Memgraph GraphRAG, dynamic context, permission-aware retrieval, and memory boundaries.

## Stable v1 boundaries

See [Compatibility and versioning](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/compatibility-and-versioning) for supported versions, reviewed baselines, and the v0 to v1 migration boundary.

- Construct agents, pipelines, and extractors directly; builder-era APIs are migration context only.
- Use `@anvia/mcp` for MCP SDK v2 clients and transports. Core retains lightweight registration contracts.
- Use Client Protocol v3 across `@anvia/client`, `@anvia/server`, and `@anvia/react`.
- Treat the `@anvia/react` primitives as strictly headless. Use the CLI component guide (`pnpm dlx @anvia/cli ui add chat`) for
  editable application-owned UI. The CLI also installs coding-agent skills; the bundled `anvia-*` skills are
  manual-invocation only (for example `/anvia-agent` or `$anvia-agent`).
- Parse files or run OCR in application code, then pass normalized text to Core document helpers.
  Provider adapters may separately support PDF attachments for model input.
- Treat Anvia package versions independently and verify declared dependency ranges instead of
  requiring one synchronized version number.
- Keep retrieval permissions, tool authorization, interaction continuations, and public-event projection on the server.
- Use Lens and Core evals for trace-correlated, versioned release evidence; deployment policy remains application-owned.

## Start Here

- [Introduction](https://docs.anvia.dev/): What Anvia is, the products, and where to start.
- [What is an agent runtime?](https://docs.anvia.dev/guide/introduction): Anvia's role in an application, the responsibilities it leaves to the host application, and the package map.
- [Add Anvia to your coding agent](https://docs.anvia.dev/guide/coding-agents): Install CLI Agent Skills for Claude Code, Cursor, or AGENTS.md/Codex, and use these LLM text guides.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.anvia.dev/guide/getting-started): Install the smallest runtime stack and run a first agent.
- [Core concepts](https://docs.anvia.dev/guide/core-concepts): Models, agents, tools, memory, knowledge, pipelines, streaming, and runtime events.
- [Configuration](https://docs.anvia.dev/guide/configuration): Environment and runtime configuration guidance.

## Features

- [Agent Runtime](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/agent-runtime): Agent construction, generate and stream, run outcomes, limits, and per-run overrides.
- [Agent API and interfaces](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/agent-api): Serve an agent from an HTTP route and render it in React.
- [Tools and MCP](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/tools-and-mcp): Typed tools, approvals, tool indexes and search, MCP servers, and skills.
- [Knowledge and RAG](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/knowledge-and-rag): Context documents, embeddings, vector stores, retrieval, and GraphRAG.
- [Memory](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/memory): Memory stores, session scope, save policies, and compaction.
- [Multi-agent teams](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/multi-agent): Coordinating specialist agents and when to use pipelines instead.
- [Durable execution](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/durable-execution): Runs that survive restarts, recorded steps, and durable stores.
- [Channels](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/channels): Connecting agents to messaging platforms.
- [Security and auth](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/security): Authenticate, authorize, bound, and observe Anvia-based systems for real users.
- [Observability](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/observability): Runtime logging, traces, scores, and Lens.
- [Evaluations](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/evaluations): Offline suites, scoring, datasets, and release gates.
- [Studio](https://docs.anvia.dev/features/studio): Local inspection of agents, sessions, traces, tools, and memory.

## SDK

- [SDK overview](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/): Package map and recommended routes through the SDK documentation.
- [Install and setup](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/install-and-setup): SDK installation and provider setup.
- [Your first agent](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/your-first-agent): Minimal typed agent example.
- [Models](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/models): Model abstractions and supported model capabilities.
- [Completions](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/completions): Direct model completion APIs.
- [Agents](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/agents): Agent construction, instructions, context, lifecycle, and limits.
- [Messages](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/messages): Message roles and content types.
- [Tools](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/tools): Typed tools, validation, execution, middleware, and security.
- [Memory](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/memory): Sessions, persistence policies, compaction, and store adapters.
- [Versioned memory writes](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/memory/versioned-writes): Idempotency keys, optimistic versions, conflicts, and durable recorded memory.
- [Knowledge](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/knowledges): Document loading, embeddings, vector stores, retrieval, and search tools.
- [Structured output](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/structured-output): Schema-driven completion and agent output.
- [Typed decisions](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/decisions): Bounded classification, routing, scoring, and verification questions with typed answers.
- [Guardrails](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/guardrails): Allow, block, or rewrite model-facing input and output; separate from tool authorization.
- [Pipelines](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/pipelines): Typed multi-step workflows, composition, parallelism, and production workers.
- [Pipeline decisions and routing](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/pipelines/decisions-and-routing): Typed decision stages and choice-based routing to one branch pipeline.
- [Pipeline runs and observability](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/pipelines/runs-and-errors): Named run and stage tracing, Agent trace nesting, operational events, and failure policy.
- [Streaming](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/streaming): Completion and agent streams, event types, transports, cancellation, and resumption.
- [Providers](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/providers): OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, Grok, and compatible provider APIs; capabilities and selection.
- [Observability](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/observability): Agent observers, trace identity, lifecycle callbacks, and observer failure policy.
- [Evaluations](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/evaluations): Offline suites, agent targets, metrics, and regression gates.
- [Evaluation results](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/evaluations/results): Suite totals, `passed`, metric summaries, and per-case records.
- [Trials and caching](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/evaluations/trials-and-caching): Repeated sampling, tag filters, and target caches.
- [Evaluation CLI and baselines](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/evaluations/cli-and-baselines): CLI flags, exit codes, stored baselines, and target comparison.

## Advanced SDK Topics

- [Dynamic context](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/dynamic-context): Attach stable or request-specific context with permissions and filters.
- [Hooks and run control](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/hooks): Observe and control runtime lifecycle points.
- [Multi-agent systems](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/multi-agent): Agent composition, coordination, boundaries, and failure handling.
- [Agent teams](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/multi-agent/agent-teams): `AgentTeam` coordinators, spawned member agents, and in-flight messaging between members.
- [Durable execution](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/durable-execution): Durable workflows that survive restarts, as distinct from in-process runtime pipelines.
- [MCP](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/mcp): Connect MCP servers, map results, and define trust boundaries.
- [Agent skills](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/skills): Skill directories, `SKILL.md`, assets, loading, tools, and validation.
- [Dynamic tools](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/dynamic-tools): Large tool catalogs, indexing, embedding, and safety.
- [Domain search](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/dynamic-tools/domain-search): One search tool over plain domain entries, lexical or semantic.
- [Think tool](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/think-tool): Explicit reasoning-tool configuration and privacy guidance.
- [Sandbox execution](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/sandbox): Docker and remote sandboxes, terminals, tunnels, desktops, and security boundaries.
- [Multimodal inputs](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/multimodal): Images, audio, documents, and other media.
- [Parallel and batch work](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/advanced/parallel-and-batch): Concurrency and batch execution patterns.

## Products and Operations

- [Studio](https://docs.anvia.dev/studio/): Local runtime inspection and debugging.
- [Run your first agent in Studio](https://docs.anvia.dev/studio/run-your-first-agent): Initial Studio workflow.
- [Studio sessions](https://docs.anvia.dev/studio/sessions): Inspect persisted sessions and activity.
- [Studio pipelines](https://docs.anvia.dev/studio/pipelines): Inspect and run pipelines.
- [Studio graph explorer](https://docs.anvia.dev/studio/graphs): Inspect bounded Neo4j and Memgraph graph views.
- [Lens](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/): Production observability and evaluation.
- [Install and set up Lens](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/install-and-setup): Connect an application to Lens.
- [Your first trace](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/your-first-trace): Capture and inspect runtime telemetry.
- [Configure Lens tracing](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/connect/anvia/configure-tracing): Create one Lens tracing instance at startup from environment variables or explicit options.
- [Lens evaluations](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/evaluations): Runs, results, datasets, comparison, and quality gates.
- [Evaluation metrics](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/evaluations/metrics): Every `@anvia/core/evals` metric, score keys, judge settings, and invalid results.
- [Lens evidence policies](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/evaluations/quality-gates/configure#require-valid-evidence-per-metric): Per-metric valid-case minimums and invalid/unknown budgets.
- [Lens observability](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/observability): Traces, sessions, users, costs, and alerts.
- [Lens self-hosting](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/self-hosting/architecture): Self-hosted architecture and operational guidance.
- [Lens prompt management](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/prompts): Immutable prompt versions and mutable deployment labels.
- [Lens workspace](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/workspace): Workspace-wide member access; projects are not human-access isolation boundaries.
- [Lens OIDC and SSO](https://docs.anvia.dev/lens/workspace/oidc): Provider configuration, invitations, provisioning, and recovery.
- [Channels](https://docs.anvia.dev/channels/): Discord, Slack, and Telegram adapters that connect platforms to agents and support proactive delivery.
- [Channels end-to-end guide](https://docs.anvia.dev/channels/end-to-end): `createChannelAgent()` with `discord()`, `slack()`, or `telegram()`; durable interactions with `SqliteChannelAgentInteractionStore`; proactive `sendChannelMessage()`.
- [Discord](https://docs.anvia.dev/channels/discord), [Slack](https://docs.anvia.dev/channels/slack), and [Telegram](https://docs.anvia.dev/channels/telegram): Platform adapter setup, scopes or intents, receiving, and messaging.
- [Channel core](https://docs.anvia.dev/channels/channel): `sendChannelMessage()`, `splitChannelMessage()`, `createRateLimitedChannel()`, and `PartialDeliveryError`.
- [Channel-agent commands](https://docs.anvia.dev/channels/channel-agent/commands): Opt-in slash commands; commands skip the message filter, so authorize them with `commands.shouldHandle`.

## Packages

- [Package catalog](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/): Published packages and their roles.
- [Compatibility and versioning](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/compatibility-and-versioning): Independent package versions, reviewed baselines, and the v0 to v1 migration boundary.
- [`@anvia/core`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/core): Core runtime APIs for models, agents, tools, messages, and pipelines.
- [`@anvia/client`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/client): Framework-neutral Client Protocol v3 types, transports, and client-state reduction.
- [`@anvia/server`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/server): Server transports and streaming integration.
- [`@anvia/react`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/react): React state and hooks for Anvia streams.
- [React primitives](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/react/capabilities): Strictly headless React interface primitives that ship with `@anvia/react`.
- [`@anvia/durable`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/durable): Persisted model and tool checkpoints, submission, observation, and recovery after restarts.
- [Durable goals](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/durable/goals): Verified objectives across bounded sessions, continuing rounds, budgets, and pause/edit/message signals.
- [Durable compaction](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/durable/compaction): Registration-level summaries and recoverable active-loop projections without deleting canonical history.
- [Durable steering](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/durable/steering): Persisted user input and deduplicated receipts at safe execution boundaries.
- [Durable tracing](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/durable/tracing): Stable run traces, application chat grouping, and OpenTelemetry ID-generator setup.
- [`@anvia/mcp`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/mcp): MCP SDK v2 clients, transports, discovery, and lifecycle ownership.
- [`@anvia/sandbox`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/sandbox): Docker-backed workspaces, remote runtime, in-sandbox daemon, virtual desktop, and sandbox tools.
- [`@anvia/studio`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/studio): Studio development UI and HTTP runtime around registered agents, pipelines, and graph explorers.
- [`@anvia/cli`](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/cli): Coding-agent skills and editable shadcn/Tailwind application components.
- [CLI Agent Skills](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/cli/agent-skills): Ten bundled manual-invocation skills (including experimental anvia-durable), Claude Code, Cursor, AGENTS.md/Codex, custom directories, and target-specific updates.
- [CLI editable components](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/cli/components): Registry items, optional explicit `@anvia/react` version pinning, controller wiring, and shared-file updates.
- [OpenAI decisions](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/openai/decisions): Choice, score, check, multi-label mappings, request limits, and typed refusals.
- [Memory adapters](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/memory/store-adapters): SQLite, PostgreSQL, Drizzle, and Prisma-backed memory.
- [Vector stores](https://docs.anvia.dev/sdk/knowledges/vector-stores): Qdrant, Pinecone, pgvector, Redis, Chroma, LanceDB, Milvus, and Weaviate.
- [Knowledge graphs](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/graph): Portable graph contracts plus Neo4j and Memgraph adapters.
- [Observability integrations](https://docs.anvia.dev/packages/): Logger, OpenTelemetry, Lens, and Langfuse packages.

CLI guides document CLI 1.5.8: the `ui` and `skills` command groups, read-only update previews with `--apply` (introduced in 1.4.0), and manual-invocation bundled skills (1.5.8). Root `init`, `add`, and `update` remain aliases.

## Examples

- [Examples index](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/): Runnable patterns organized by use case.
- [Golden path tutorial](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/golden-path): One production-shaped app: a Discord agent with typed tools, durable memory, Lens traces, and a proactive report.
- [Essentials](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/essentials/first-agent): First agents, completions, memory, tools, streaming, and structured output.
- [Agents and tools](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/agents-and-tools/tool-calling): Tool calling, approvals, permissions, middleware, cancellation, and multi-agent composition.
- [Knowledge and data](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/knowledge-and-data/basic-rag): Retrieval, document ingestion, metadata filters, memory, and vector-store adapters.
- [Providers and media](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/providers-and-media/provider-switching): Provider switching, compatible APIs, images, audio, PDF, OCR, and live search.
- [Data and workflows](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/data-and-workflows/research-pipeline): Pipelines, batch work, background jobs, recovery, and human review.
- [Applications](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/applications/streaming-react-chat): End-to-end application examples.
- [Production](https://docs.anvia.dev/examples/production/authentication): Authentication, tracing, retries, limits, testing, evaluations, and quality gates.
